title: 〜ならまだしも
meaning: if it were X, that would still be acceptable, but (the actual case is worse)
simpleExplanation: 〜ならまだしも presents a milder case that the speaker could have tolerated, then complains that what actually happened is worse. 一度ならまだしも、三度も = "Once would be one thing, but three times!". まだしも means "still better". The tone is annoyed or disappointed.
whenUsed: Spoken and written, common in complaints and criticism. X is the tolerable case (一度・子供・少し・知らなかったの); the second half is the intolerable reality, often ending in とは / なんて / のは問題だ.
formation: 普通形 + の + ならまだしも  (知らなかったのならまだしも)
いA / なA + ならまだしも  (安いならまだしも・少しならまだしも)
Second half: the worse reality + とは / なんて / のは困る

items.description: once: I could still let it go

examples.ja: 一度ならまだしも、三度も同じ失敗をするとは。
examples.reading: いちどならまだしも、さんどもおなじしっぱいをするとは。
examples.en: Once would be one thing, but making the same mistake three times...
examples.note: Once is tolerable; three times crosses the line.

examples.ja: 子供ならまだしも、大人がそんな言い訳をするなんて。
examples.reading: こどもならまだしも、おとながそんないいわけをするなんて。
examples.en: A child might be excused, but for an adult to make such an excuse...
examples.note: 子供ならまだしも: a child could be excused; an adult cannot.

examples.ja: 遅れるだけならまだしも、連絡もしないのは失礼だ。
examples.reading: おくれるだけならまだしも、れんらくもしないのはしつれいだ。
examples.en: Being late would be one thing, but not even getting in touch is rude.
examples.note: 遅れるだけならまだしも: mere lateness is forgivable; not calling is not.

examples.ja: 少し値上げするならまだしも、いきなり倍になるなんてひどい。
examples.reading: すこしねあげするならまだしも、いきなりばいになるなんてひどい。
examples.en: A small price rise would be one thing, but doubling it out of nowhere is awful.
examples.note: The worse reality ends in なんてひどい.

examples.ja: 初心者ならまだしも、経験者がこんな基本的なミスをするとは。
examples.reading: しょしんしゃならまだしも、けいけんしゃがこんなきほんてきなミスをするとは。
examples.en: From a beginner it might be understandable, but for an experienced person to make such a basic mistake…
examples.note: Sentence-final とは leaves the disapproval hanging.

similarGrammar.difference: Also "if it were X, fine, but". ともかく is more neutral ("setting X aside"); まだしも stresses that X would have been tolerable, so the contrast is more emotional.
"I don't know about X, but" — sets aside an unknown or extreme case. まだしも sets aside a mild case the speaker could accept.
Puts a topic aside to focus on another ("never mind X"). Not a scale from tolerable to intolerable.

commonMistakes.wrong: 三度ならまだしも、一度失敗した。
commonMistakes.right: 一度ならまだしも、三度も失敗した。
commonMistakes.why: X must be the milder, tolerable case, and the reality the worse one. Reversing them makes no sense.

commonMistakes.wrong: 遅刻するならまだしも、早く来た。
commonMistakes.right: 遅刻するならまだしも、来ないのは困る。
commonMistakes.why: The second half must be worse than X. Arriving early is not a complaint.

commonMistakes.wrong: 子供のならまだしも、大人がそんな言い訳をするなんて。
commonMistakes.right: 子供ならまだしも、大人がそんな言い訳をするなんて。
commonMistakes.why: A noun attaches directly with なら. The の is only needed after a verb or い-adjective (知らなかったのならまだしも).

usageNotes: The intolerable half is often marked by も (三度も), まで, or なんて to stress excess.
It can be used in self-criticism too: 学生の頃ならまだしも、この年で徹夜はきつい.
In polite complaints, まだしも softens by admitting the speaker would have accepted a milder version.
jlptTips: In 文法形式の判断, look for a pair on a scale (一度 vs 三度, 子供 vs 大人, 少し vs 倍) with an annoyed ending; that is ならまだしも.
If the options include ならともかく and ならまだしも, both may be grammatical; まだしも is the one that emphasizes "X was still bearable".
In 並べ替え, ならまだしも is one chunk; the milder case sits before it, the worse case after.
